items.e: The spirit of prophecy from before Hashem rested upon me, and brought me out by the spirit of prophecy that rested upon me from before Hashem, and set me down in the midst of the valley, and it was full of human bones.
And He caused me to pass by them all around, and behold, there were very many upon the face of the valley, and behold, they were very dry.
And He said to me: "Ben adam, can these bones live?" And I said: "Hashem Elokim, it is revealed before You."
And He said to me: "Prophesy over these bones, and say to them: O dry bones, accept the word of Hashem!
Thus said Hashem Elokim to these bones: Behold, I am bringing a spirit into you, and you shall live.
And I will put sinews upon you, and bring up flesh upon you, and cover you with skin, and put a spirit in you, and you shall live; and you shall know that I am Hashem."
So I prophesied as I was commanded, and there was a sound as I prophesied, and behold, a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to its bone.
And I looked, and behold, there were sinews upon them, and flesh came up, and skin covered them from above, but there was no spirit in them.
Then He said to me: "Prophesy to the spirit; prophesy, ben adam, and say to the spirit: Thus said Hashem Elokim: Come from the four winds, O spirit, and enter into these slain, that they may live!"
So I prophesied as He commanded me, and the spirit entered into them, and they came to life, and stood upon their feet, an exceedingly great army.
And He said to me: "Ben adam, these bones are all the house of Yisrael; behold, they say, 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost, we are completely cut off!'
Therefore prophesy, and say to them: Thus said Hashem Elokim: Behold, I am opening your graves, and I will raise you up from your graves, My people, and I will bring you into the land of Yisrael.
And you shall know that I am Hashem, when I open your graves, and when I raise you up from your graves, My people.
And I will put My spirit in you, and you shall live, and I will settle you upon your land; and you shall know that I, Hashem, have decreed by My word, and I will fulfill it, says Hashem."
And the word of nevuah from before Hashem was with me, saying:

"And you, ben adam, take for yourself one tablet, and write upon it: 'For the tribe of Yehudah, and for the Bnei Yisrael his brethren.' And take another tablet, and write upon it: 'For the tribe of Yosef, which is the tribe of Efraim, and all the house of Yisrael his brethren.'
And bring them close, one to the other, for yourself into one tablet, and they shall be joined together in your hand.
And when the children of your people say to you, 'Will you not tell us what these mean for you?'

Prophesy to them: Thus said Hashem Elokim: Behold, I am bringing near the tribe of Yosef, which is the tribe of Efraim, and the tribes of Yisrael his brethren, and I will join them upon him, upon the tribe of Yehudah, and I will make them one people, and they shall be one before Me.
And the tablets upon which you write shall be in your hand before their eyes.

And prophesy to them: Thus said Hashem Elokim: Behold, I am bringing near the Bnei Yisrael from among the nations where they were exiled, and I will gather them from all around, and bring them into their own land.

And I will make them one nation in the land, upon the holy mountain of Yisrael, and one king shall be king over them all; and they shall no longer be two nations, nor shall they ever be divided into two kingdoms again.

And they shall no longer defile themselves with their sins, nor with their abominations, nor with all their rebellions; and I will save them from all their dwelling places where they sinned before Me, and I will cleanse them, and they shall be a people before Me, and I will be a God to them.
And My servant David shall be king over them, and one leader shall be for them all; and in My judgments they shall walk, and My statutes they shall keep and perform them.

And they shall dwell upon the land that I gave to My servant Yaakov, in which your fathers dwelt; and they shall dwell upon it, they, and their children, and their children's children forever; and David My servant shall be a king over them forever.
And I will make with them a covenant of peace; an everlasting covenant it shall be with them; and I will bless them and multiply them, and I will set My Sanctuary in their midst forever.
And I will place My Shechinah in their midst, and I will be a God to them, and they shall be a people before Me.
And the nations shall know that I am Hashem who sanctifies Yisrael, when My Sanctuary is in their midst forever."
And the word of nevuah from before Hashem was with me, saying:
"Ben adam, accept nevuah concerning Gog of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tuval, and prophesy against him.
And say: Thus said Hashem Elokim: Behold, I am sending My anger against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tuval.

And I will entice you, and put hooks into your jaws, and bring you out with all your army—horses and horsemen, all of them fully clothed, a great assembly equipped with bucklers and shields, all of them handling swords.
Persians, Cushites, and Putites with them, all of them equipped with bucklers and helmets.
Gomer and all her armies, the province of Germania from the uttermost north and all their armies—many nations with you.
Be prepared and make yourself ready, you and all your armies that are gathered unto you, and be a guard for them.

After many days your armies shall be numbered; in the end of years you shall come against the land that has been restored from those killed by the sword, gathered from many nations upon the mountains of the land of Yisrael, which had been a continual waste; but they were brought out from among the nations, and all of them dwell in security.
And you shall ascend in a tumult; you shall come like a cloud that rises and covers the land, you and all your armies, and many nations with you.
Thus said Hashem Elokim: And it shall come to pass at that time that thoughts shall arise in your heart, and you shall devise evil schemes.
And you shall say, 'I will go up against an open land; I will come upon a quiet people who dwell in security, all of them dwelling without walls, having no bars or gates,'

To plunder spoil and carry off booty, to turn your hand against the inhabited ruins and against the people gathered from among the nations, who have acquired possessions and property, who dwell upon the strength of the land.

Sheva, Dedan, the merchants of the sea, and all her kings shall say to you, 'Have you come to plunder spoil? Have you gathered your assembly to carry off booty, to take away silver and gold, to seize possessions and property, to take great spoil?'
Therefore, ben adam, prophesy and say to Gog: Thus said Hashem Elokim: Surely at that time, when My people Yisrael dwell in security, you shall know the retribution of My power!
And you shall come from your place out of the uttermost north, you and many nations with you, all of them riding upon horses, a great assembly and a mighty army.

And you shall come up against My people Yisrael like a cloud that rises and covers the land; in the end of days it shall be, and I will bring you against the land of My Shechinah's dwelling, so that the nations may know the retribution of My power when I am sanctified through you before their eyes, O Gog!

Thus said Hashem Elokim: Are you the one of whom I spoke in ancient days by the hand of My servants, the prophets of Yisrael, who prophesied in those days many years ago, that I would bring you against them?
And it shall come to pass on that day, on the day that Gog comes against the land of Yisrael, says Hashem Elokim, that My anger and My wrath shall blaze up.
And in the manifestation of My retribution, in the blazing fire of My wrath, I have decreed by My word: Surely on that day there shall be a great shaking upon the land of Yisrael!

And the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, the beasts of the field, all creeping things that creep upon the earth, and all human beings upon the face of the earth shall shake before Me; and the mountains shall be thrown down, the towers shall fall, and every high wall shall collapse to the ground.
And I will summon against him a sword upon all the mountains of My people Yisrael, says Hashem Elokim; every man's sword shall be against his brother.

And I will execute retribution upon him with pestilence and with slaughter; and overflowing rain, great hailstones, fire, and brimstone will I rain upon him, upon his armies, and upon the many nations that are with him.
Thus will I magnify Myself and sanctify Myself, and make My power known in the eyes of many nations; and they shall know that I am Hashem."
"And you, ben adam, prophesy concerning Gog, and say: Thus said Hashem Elokim: Behold, I am sending My anger against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tuval.
And I will entice you and lead you astray, and bring you up from the uttermost north, and bring you against the mountains of Yisrael.
And I will strike your bow from your left hand, and make your arrows fall from your right hand.

Upon the mountains of the land of Yisrael your carcass shall fall, you and all your armies, and the nations that are with you; to the bird of every wing and to the beasts of the field I have delivered you to be consumed.
Upon the open field your carcass shall fall; for I have decreed it by My word, says Hashem Elokim.
And I will send fire upon Magog and upon the inhabitants of the islands who dwell in security; and they shall know that I am Hashem.

And My holy name I will make known in the midst of My people Yisrael, and I will no longer let My holy name be profaned; and the nations shall know that I am Hashem, the Holy One who has placed My Shechinah in Yisrael.
Behold, it is coming and it shall be fulfilled, says Hashem Elokim; this is the day of which I have decreed by My word.

And the inhabitants of the cities of the land of Yisrael shall go forth, and they shall kindle fires and make use of the weapons—the bucklers and shields, the bows and arrows, the hand-staves and spears; and they shall kindle fires with them for seven years.

So that they shall take no wood from the field, nor cut down any from the forests, for they shall kindle fires with the weapons; and they shall plunder those who plundered them, and spoil those who spoiled them, says Hashem Elokim.

And it shall come to pass on that day that I will give Gog a place suited for a burial site in Yisrael—the valley of those who pass through, east of the Sea of Ginosar, adjacent to the two mountains; and there they shall bury Gog and all his crowd, and they shall call it the Valley of Gog's Crowd.
And seven months shall the house of Yisrael be burying them, in order to cleanse the land.
All the people of the land shall bury them, and it shall bring them renown on the day I am glorified, says Hashem Elokim.

And they shall appoint men continually to pass through the land, burying with those who pass through those that remain upon the face of the earth, to cleanse it; at the end of seven months they shall begin to search.
And those who pass through the land shall pass through, and if anyone sees a human bone, he shall build a marker beside it until the buriers have buried it in the Valley of Gog's Crowd.
And there also shall be cast the slain of Rome, the city of many crowds, O Gog; and they shall cleanse the land.

And you, ben adam, thus said Hashem Elokim: Say to the bird of every wing and to every beast of the field: Assemble and come, gather yourselves from all around to the slaughter that I am slaughtering for you, a great slaughter upon the mountains of Yisrael, that you may eat flesh and drink blood.
The flesh of warriors you shall eat, and the blood of the princes of the earth you shall drink—kings, rulers, tyrants, warriors, and all men wealthy in possessions.
And you shall eat fat till you are full, and drink blood till you are drunk, from the flesh of the slain that I slaughter for you.
And you shall be filled at My table upon the mountains of Yisrael with horses, chariots, warriors, and all men of war, says Hashem Elokim.
And I will set My glory among the nations, and all the nations shall see My retribution which I have executed, and My power which I have set upon them.
So the house of Yisrael shall know that I am Hashem their God, from that day forward.

And the nations shall know that for their sins the house of Yisrael went into exile, because they acted falsely against My word; therefore I removed My Shechinah from them and delivered them into the hand of their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
According to their uncleanness and according to their rebellions I took retribution from them, and I removed My Shechinah from them.

Therefore, thus said Hashem Elokim: Now I will restore the captivity of Yaakov, and have mercy upon the whole house of Yisrael, and execute the retribution of My power upon the nations because they profaned My holy name.
And they shall bear their submissiveness and all their falsehood which they committed against My word, when they dwell upon their land in security, with no one to terrify them.
When I bring them back from among the nations and gather them out of the lands of their enemies, and am sanctified through them in the sight of many nations;

Then they shall know that I am Hashem their God, in that because they sinned before Me I exiled them among the nations, but now that they have repented I have gathered them into their land, and I will leave none of them behind anymore.
Neither will I ever remove My Shechinah from them again, for I have poured out My Holy Spirit upon the house of Yisrael, says Hashem Elokim."

In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck down, on this selfsame day the spirit of prophecy from before Hashem rested upon me and brought me there.

In the spirit of prophecy that rested upon me from before Him, He brought me to the land of Yisrael and set me down upon a very high mountain, and upon it was like the structure of a city from the south.
And He brought me there, and behold, there was a man whose appearance was like the appearance of copper, with a cord of linen in his hand and a measuring reed, standing in the gateway.

And the man spoke to me: "Ben adam, see with your eyes, hear with your ears, and set your heart to all that I am showing you, for in order to show you were you brought here; go and declare all that you see to the house of Yisrael."

And behold, there was a wall outside the House all around; and in the man's hand was a measuring reed of six cubits, each cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth. So he measured the width of the building, one reed; and the height, one reed.
Then he came to the gateway facing east and climbed its steps, and measured the threshold of the gate, one reed wide; and the other threshold, one reed wide.
And each cell was one reed long and one reed wide, and between the cells was a space of five cubits; and the threshold of the gate by the vestibule of the gate facing inward was one reed.
He also measured the vestibule of the gate facing inward, one reed.
Then he measured the vestibule of the gate, eight cubits; and its posts, two cubits; and the vestibule of the gate was facing inward.
And the cells of the gate facing east were three on this side and three on that side—the three had one measurement, and the posts on this side and on that side had one measurement.
He measured the width of the entrance of the gate, ten cubits; and the length of the gate, thirteen cubits.
And the space before the cells was one cubit on this side and one cubit on that side, and each cell was six cubits on this side and six cubits on that side.
He measured the gate from the roof of one cell to the roof of another, a width of twenty-five cubits, door facing door.
And he made the posts sixty cubits high, and by the post was the courtyard of the gate all around.
And from the front of the entry gate to the front of the inner vestibule of the gate was fifty cubits.

There were narrow windows to the cells and to their posts facing inward all around the gate, and likewise to the vestibules; and windows were all around facing inward, and upon each post were palm trees.
Then he brought me into the outer courtyard, and behold, there were chambers and a pavement made for the courtyard all around; thirty chambers were upon the pavement.
And the pavement was at the side of the gates, corresponding to the length of the gates—the lower pavement.
He measured the width from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner courtyard on the outside, one hundred cubits eastward and northward.
And as for the gate facing north in the outer courtyard, he measured its length and its width.
Its cells were three on this side and three on that side; and its posts and its vestibules had the same measurements as the first gate: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its windows, its vestibules, and its palm trees had the same measurements as the gate facing east; and they climbed up to it by seven steps, with its vestibule before them.
And a gate to the inner courtyard was opposite the gate facing north and facing east; and he measured from gate to gate, one hundred cubits.
Then he led me toward the south, and behold, there was a gate facing south; and he measured its posts and its vestibules according to these measurements.
There were windows in it and in its vestibules all around, like those windows: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its steps were seven steps, with its vestibule before them; and it had palm trees on its posts, one on this side and one on that side.
And there was a gate to the inner courtyard facing south; and he measured from gate to gate facing south, one hundred cubits.
Then he brought me to the inner courtyard through the south gate, and he measured the south gate according to these measurements.
Its cells, its posts, and its vestibules were according to these measurements; and there were windows in it and in its vestibules all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
And the vestibules all around were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
Its vestibules faced the outer courtyard, with palm trees upon its posts; and its steps were eight steps.
Then he brought me into the inner courtyard toward the east, and he measured the gate according to these measurements.
Its cells, its posts, and its vestibules were according to these measurements; and there were windows in it and in its vestibules all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its vestibules faced the outer courtyard, with palm trees upon its posts on this side and on that side; and its steps were eight steps.
Then he brought me to the north gate and measured it according to these measurements:
Its cells, its posts, its vestibules, and its windows all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its posts faced the outer courtyard, with palm trees upon its posts on this side and on that side; and its steps were eight steps.
And a chamber with its doorway was by the posts of the gates, where they prepare the burnt offerings.
And in the vestibule of the gate were two tables on this side and two tables on that side, on which to slaughter the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.
On the outer side, as one goes up to the entrance of the north gate, were two tables; and on the other side of the vestibule of the gate were two tables.
Four tables on this side and four tables on that side, by the side of the gate—eight tables, upon which they slaughter the offerings.

And there were four tables for the burnt offering of hewn stones, a cubit and a half long, a cubit and a half wide, and one cubit high, upon which they place the instruments with which they slaughter the burnt offering and the holy sacrifices.
And hooks of one handbreadth were fastened within the slaughterhouse all around the vestibules; and upon the tables was the flesh of the offerings.
And outside the inner gate were chambers for the Levites in the inner courtyard, one at the side of the north gate facing south, and one at the side of the east gate facing north.
And he spoke to me: "This chamber facing south is for the kohanim who keep the charge of the House.

And the chamber facing north is for the kohanim who keep the charge of the Altar; these are the sons of Tzadok, who alone among the sons of Levi draw near to the service of Hashem to minister before Him."
So he measured the courtyard, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide, square; and the Altar was before the House.

Then he brought me to the vestibule of the House and measured each post of the vestibule, five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side; and the width of the gate was three cubits on this side and three cubits on that side.
The length of the vestibule was twenty cubits, and by steps they climbed up to it; and there were pillars by the posts, one on this side and one on that side.
And he brought me into the Main Hall (the *Heichal*) and measured the posts, which were six cubits wide on each side, matching the width of the Structure.

The width of the doorway was ten cubits, and the side-walls of the entrance were five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other. He measured its length as forty cubits and its width as twenty cubits.
Then he went further inside and measured the post of the inner doorway: two cubits, with the doorway itself being six cubits wide and the entrance's side-walls seven cubits.
He measured its length as twenty cubits and its width as twenty cubits before the Hall, and said to me: "This is the Holy of Holies (*Beis Kodesh HaKodashim*)."
He then measured the wall of the House: six cubits thick. The width of the side-chambers (*tzelaos*) surrounding the House all around was four cubits.

The side-chambers were arranged one above another, thirty-three in total, in three tiers of eleven. They were set into the outer wall of the House to support the beams without having the structural beams penetrate directly into the main walls of the House itself.
The side-chambers broadened as they wound upward tier by tier around the House, allowing access from the lowest level to the highest via a winding middle stairwell.
I saw that the House had an elevated foundation all around, measuring a full reed of six large cubits.
The outer wall of the side-chambers was five cubits thick, with an open courtyard space left between the inner side-chambers and the outer chambers.
Between these chambers and the outer structures was an open space of twenty cubits surrounding the House on every side.
The doorways of the side-chambers opened onto this clear space—one facing north and one facing south—and the surrounding clear space was five cubits wide.
The western building facing the separate area (*Bizrah*) was seventy cubits wide, surrounded by a five-cubit thick wall, and was ninety cubits long.
He measured the overall length of the House as one hundred cubits, including the separate area, the building, and its walls.
The eastern width of the front of the House and the separate area was also one hundred cubits.
He measured the rear length of the building facing the separate area, including its galleries on both sides, as one hundred cubits, along with the Inner Hall and the vestibules of the courtyard.
The thresholds, narrow windows, and surrounding galleries on three sides were paneled with cedar wood from the floor up to the windows (which were lattice-covered).
The space above the doorway, the inner and outer areas, and all along the walls were covered with detailed carvings.
Carved throughout were cherubim and palm trees—a palm tree between every two cherubim—and each cherub had two faces:
A human face facing the palm tree on one side, and a lion's face facing the palm tree on the other side, carved continuously all around the House.
From the floor to above the doorway, cherubim and palm trees were carved into the walls of the Main Hall.
The doorposts of the Main Hall were square, and the entrance to the Holy of Holies had a similar appearance.
The wooden Altar was three cubits high and two cubits long, with its corners, length, and walls made of wood. He said to me: "This is the Table that stands before Hashem."
Both the Main Hall and the Holy of Holies had double doors.
Each door had two folding leaves—two for one door and two for the other.
Carved upon the doors of the Main Hall were cherubim and palm trees, matching those on the walls, with a wooden canopy over the front of the vestibule outside.
There were narrow windows and palm tree decorations on both side-walls of the vestibule, as well as on the side-chambers of the House and the canopies.
Then he led me out into the outer courtyard by way of the gate facing north, and brought me to the chambers facing the separate area (*Bizrah*) and the building to the north.
Along the hundred-cubit length was the doorway facing north, and the width was fifty cubits.
Opposite the twenty-cubit space of the inner courtyard and opposite the pavement of the outer courtyard facing north were galleries facing galleries in three tiers.
In front of the chambers was an inner walkway ten cubits wide, a path of one cubit, and their doorways faced north.
The upper chambers were narrower because the galleries took away space from them compared to the lower and middle stories of the building.
For they were three stories high, but lacked pillars like the pillars of the courtyards; therefore the upper tier was set back more than the lower and middle tiers from the ground.
An outer wall parallel to the chambers toward the outer courtyard, in front of the chambers, was fifty cubits long.
For the length of the chambers facing the outer courtyard was fifty cubits, while the total facade facing the Main Hall was one hundred cubits.
Below these chambers was the eastern entrance for entering them from the outer courtyard.
Along the thickness of the courtyard wall toward the east, in front of the separate area and the building, were chambers.
There was a walkway in front of them similar in appearance to the chambers facing north: matching their length, width, all their exits, arrangements, and doorways.
Like the doorways of the chambers facing south, there was an entrance at the head of the pathway—the path in front of the Levites' platform facing east as one enters them.

He said to me: "The northern chambers and southern chambers in front of the separate area are the holy chambers where the kohanim who draw near to serve before Hashem eat the holy of holies; there they shall place the holy of holies, the meal offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, for the place is holy.

When the kohanim enter, they shall not go out from the Holy Place into the outer courtyard without placing there their official vestments in which they minister—for they are holy—and putting on other garments before mingling with the people."
When he had finished measuring the inner House, he led me out by way of the gate facing east, and measured the outer perimeter all around.
He measured the eastern side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds with the measuring reed, all around.
He measured the northern side: five hundred reeds with the measuring reed, all around.
He measured the southern side: five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.
He turned to the western side and measured: five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.
He measured it on all four sides; it had a surrounding wall five hundred reeds long and five hundred reeds wide, to separate between the holy and the profane.
And he led me to the gate, the gate facing east.

And behold, the glory of the God of Yisrael was revealed from the way of the east; and the voice of those who bless His name was like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone with the splendor of His glory.
And the appearance of the vision that I saw was like the vision I had seen in my prophecy when I came to destroy the city, and like the vision I had seen by the river Kevar; and I fell upon my face.
And the glory of Hashem was revealed in the House by way of the gate facing east.
And a spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner courtyard; and behold, the House was filled with the glory of Hashem.
And I heard One speaking to me from within the House, and a man was standing beside me.

And He said to me: "Ben adam, this is the place of the throne of My glory, and this is the place of the dwelling of My Shechinah, where I will place My Shechinah in the midst of the Bnei Yisrael forever; and the house of Yisrael shall no longer defile My holy name—they and their kings—with their idol worship and with the corpses of their kings in their high places.

In setting their thresholds near My thresholds and their posts beside My posts, with only a wall between My word and them, they defiled My holy name with their abominations that they committed; wherefore I consumed them in My anger.
Now let them put away their idol worship and the corpses of their kings far from sinning before Me, and I will place My Shechinah in their midst forever.
You, ben adam, show the house of Yisrael the House, that they may be humbled by their sins, and let them measure its design.

And if they are humbled by all that they have done, make known to them the form of the House and its arrangement, its exits and its entrances, its total design, all its decrees, its forms, and all that pertains to it; write it before their eyes, so that they may keep its total design and all its decrees, and perform them.
This is the law of the House: Upon the top of the mountain, its entire border all around shall be holy of holies. Behold, this is the law of the House!

And these are the measurements of the Altar in cubits—the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: the base shall be a cubit high and a cubit wide, with a border along its edge all around of one span; and this is the base of the Altar.
From the base on the ground to the lower ledge shall be two cubits, and the width one cubit; and from the lesser ledge to the greater ledge shall be four cubits, and the width one cubit.
And the Altar hearth shall be four cubits high; and from the Altar hearth upward shall be four horns.
And the Altar hearth shall be twelve cubits long by twelve cubits wide, square on its four sides.
And the ledge shall be fourteen cubits long by fourteen cubits wide on its four sides, with a border around it of half a cubit, and its base a cubit all around; and its steps shall face east."

And He said to me: "Ben adam, thus said Hashem Elokim: These are the decrees of the Altar on the day it is made, to offer burnt offerings upon it and to sprinkle the blood of the holy sacrifices upon it.
You shall give to the kohanim who are Levites of the seed of Tzadok, who draw near to My service, says Hashem Elokim, to minister before Me, a young bullock for a sin offering.
And you shall take of its blood and put it on its four horns, on the four corners of the ledge, and on the border all around; thus you shall cleanse it and make atonement for it.
You shall also take the bullock of the sin offering, and burn it in the appointed place of the House, outside the Sanctuary.
And on the second day you shall offer a young buck of the goats without blemish for a sin offering; and they shall cleanse the Altar as they cleansed it with the bullock.
When you have finished cleansing it, you shall offer a young bullock without blemish, and a ram out of the flock without blemish.
And you shall offer them before Hashem, and the kohanim shall throw salt upon them, and they shall offer them up for a burnt offering before Hashem.
Seven days you shall prepare daily a goat for a sin offering; they shall also prepare a young bullock and a ram out of the flock, without blemish.
Seven days they shall make atonement for the Altar and purify it, and they shall consecrate it.

And when they complete these days, on the eighth day and onward, the kohanim shall offer upon the Altar your burnt offerings and your peace offerings; and I will accept your offerings with favor, says Hashem Elokim."
And he brought me back by way of the outer gate of the Sanctuary facing east, and it was locked.

And Hashem said to me: "This gate shall remain locked; it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter through it, for Hashem, the God of Yisrael, was revealed through it; therefore it shall remain locked.
As for the prince (*Nasi*), he—being the prince—shall sit in it to eat bread before Hashem; he shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate, and exit by the same way."
Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the House; and I looked, and behold, the glory of Hashem filled the House of Hashem, and I fell upon my face.

And Hashem said to me: "Ben adam, set your heart, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears all that I speak with you concerning all the decrees of the House of Hashem and all its laws; and set your heart to the entrances of the House and all the exits of the Sanctuary.
And say to the rebellious house of Yisrael: Thus said Hashem Elokim: Let it be enough for you of all your abominations, O house of Yisrael!

In bringing in foreigners, wicked of heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in My Sanctuary to profane My courtyard when you offer My bread, the fat, and the blood of the holy sacrifices; thus you broke My covenant in addition to all your abominations.
And you did not keep the charge of My Holy Place, but set keepers of My charge in My Sanctuary for yourselves.
Thus said Hashem Elokim: No foreigner, wicked of heart or uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter My Sanctuary—of all the foreigners who are among the Bnei Yisrael.
Rather, the Levites who went far from My fear when Yisrael strayed, who went astray from My service after their idols—they shall bear their iniquity.

And they shall be ministers in My Sanctuary, appointed over the gates of the House and ministering to the House; they shall slaughter the burnt offering and the holy sacrifices for the people, and they shall stand before them to minister to them.

Because they ministered to them before their idols and were a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Yisrael, therefore I have sworn by My word concerning them, says Hashem Elokim, that they shall bear their iniquity.
And they shall not draw near to My service to minister before Me, nor draw near to any of My holy of holies; but they shall bear their humiliation and their abominations which they committed.
Yet I will appoint them as keepers of the charge of the House, for all its service and for all that shall be done in it.

But the priests (*Kohanim*), the Levites, the sons of Tzadok, who kept the charge of My Sanctuary when the Bnei Yisrael went astray from My service—they shall draw near to My service to minister before Me, and they shall stand before Me to offer the fat and the blood of the holy sacrifices, says Hashem Elokim.
They shall enter My Sanctuary, and they shall draw near to My Table—the showbread—to minister before Me, and they shall keep the charge of My word.

And it shall be, when they enter the gates of the inner courtyard, they shall wear fine linen garments; no wool clothing shall be upon them while they minister in the gates of the inner courtyard and within.
Fine linen turbans shall be upon their heads, and fine linen trousers shall be upon their loins; they shall not gird themselves upon their loins, but shall bind them around their hearts.

And when they go out into the outer courtyard—into the outer courtyard to mingle with the people—they shall put off their vestments in which they ministered and lay them in the holy chambers, and put on other garments, so that they do not mingle with the people in their official vestments.
Neither shall they shave their heads, nor let their hair grow long; they shall trim the hair of their heads neatly.
Nor shall any Kohen drink wine when they enter the inner courtyard.
Neither a widow nor a divorced woman shall they take as wives, but only virgins of the seed of the house of Yisrael; however, a widow who is the widow of another Kohen they may marry.
And they shall teach My people the difference between the holy and the profane, and cause them to know the difference between the unclean and the clean.

And in a controversy they shall stand to judge; according to My judgments shall they judge; and My Torah and My statutes in all My appointed festivals they shall keep, and My Shabbos days they shall sanctify.
And to a dead human body they shall not come to be defiled, except for father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or unmarried sister—for these they may defile themselves.
And after he is cleansed, they shall count for him seven days.
And on the day he enters the Holy Place into the inner courtyard to minister in the Holy Place, he shall offer his sin offering, says Hashem Elokim.

And it shall be to them for an inheritance: the portion of the remainder of My offerings is their portion; no possession shall you give them in Yisrael—the gifts that I gave them are their inheritance.
The meal offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering they shall eat, and every devoted thing (*cherem*) in Yisrael shall be theirs.

And the first of all the first-fruits of everything, and every gift-offering of everything from all your gift-offerings shall belong to the Kohanim; you shall also give the first of your dough to the Kohen, to cause a blessing to rest upon your home.
The Kohanim shall not eat any carcass (*neveilah*) or torn beast (*tereifah*), whether of bird or of beast."

And when you divide the land for an inheritance, you shall set apart a holy portion (*terumah*) before Hashem from the land: the length shall be twenty-five thousand reeds, and the width ten thousand; it shall be holy in all its border all around.
Of this there shall be for the Sanctuary five hundred by five hundred reeds, square all around, with an open space (*migrash*) around it of fifty cubits.
And from this measure you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand, and in it shall be the Sanctuary, the Holy of Holies (*Kodesh Kodashim*).

This holy portion of the land belongs to the Kohanim who minister in the Sanctuary of Hashem, who draw near to minister before Hashem; and it shall be a place for their houses and a sacred area for the Sanctuary.
A area of twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width shall belong to the Levites, the ministers of the House, as their possession for twenty chambers.
And you shall assign as the possession of the city an area five thousand in width and twenty-five thousand in length, corresponding to the holy portion, for the entire house of Yisrael.

And a portion shall belong to the prince (*Nasi*) on both sides of the holy portion and the possession of the city, adjacent to the holy portion and the city's possession, on the west side westward and on the east side eastward; its length shall correspond to one of the tribal portions from the western border to the eastern border.
This land shall be his possession in Yisrael; and My princes shall no longer oppress My people, but shall give the rest of the land to the house of Yisrael according to their tribes.
Thus said Hashem Elokim: Let it be enough for you, O princes of Yisrael! Remove violence and spoil, execute justice and righteousness, and stop your exactions from My people, says Hashem Elokim.
You shall have just balances, a just *eifah*, and a just *bas*.

The *eifah* and the *bas* shall be of one measure: a *bas* shall contain three *se'ahs*—a tenth of a *kor* for liquid measure—and the *eifah* shall contain a tenth of a *kor* for dry measure; their measure shall be based on the *kor*.

And the *shekel* shall be twenty *gerahs*; a third of a *maneh* shall be twenty *shekels*, a silver *maneh* shall be twenty-five *shekels*, and a quarter of a *maneh* shall be fifteen *shekels*—making in all sixty *shekels*, which shall be the great *maneh* of the Sanctuary for you.
This is the portion (*terumah*) that you shall set apart: a sixth of an *eifah* from a *kor* of wheat, and a sixth of an *eifah* from a *kor* of barley.
And the set portion of oil for liquid measure shall be a tenth of a *bas* from a *kor*, which is ten *basses* per *kor*, for ten *basses* make a *kor*.
And one lamb out of a flock of two hundred from the fat pastures of Yisrael, for a meal offering, a burnt offering, and peace offerings, to make atonement for them, says Hashem Elokim.
All the people of the land shall give this portion for the prince in Yisrael.

And it shall be the prince's duty to provide the burnt offerings, the meal offerings, and the drink offerings at the festivals, new moons, Shabboses, and all the appointed feasts of the house of Yisrael; he shall prepare the sin offering, the meal offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make atonement for the house of Yisrael.
Thus said Hashem Elokim: In the first month, on the first day of the month, you shall take a young bullock without blemish and cleanse the Sanctuary.

And the Kohen shall take of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the House, on the four corners of the ledge of the Altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner courtyard.
And so shall you do on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins inadvertently or out of ignorance; so shall you make atonement for the House.
In Nisan, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Pesach, a festival of seven days; unleavened bread shall be eaten.
And upon that day the prince shall prepare for himself and for all the people of the land a bullock for a sin offering.

And during the seven days of the feast he shall prepare a burnt offering to Hashem: seven bullocks and seven rams without blemish daily for seven days, and a buck of the goats daily for a sin offering.
And he shall prepare a meal offering of an *eifah* for a bullock and an *eifah* for a ram, and a *hin* of oil per *eifah*.
In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the festival (Sukkos), he shall do the same for seven days—for the sin offering, the burnt offering, the meal offering, and the oil."

Thus said Hashem Elokim: The gate of the inner courtyard that faces east shall remain locked on the six working days; but on the Shabbos day it shall be opened, and on the day of the New Moon (*Rosh Chodesh*) it shall be opened.

And the prince (*Nasi*) shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate from the outside and stand by the post of the gate, while the Kohanim prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings; and he shall prostrate himself at the threshold of the gate and then go forth, but the gate shall not be locked until the evening.
And the people of the land shall prostrate themselves at the entrance of that gate on the Shabboses and on the New Moons before Hashem.
And the burnt offering that the prince shall offer to Hashem on the Shabbos day shall be six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram.
And the meal offering shall be an *eifah* for the ram, and for the lambs a meal offering according to what his hand can attain, with a *hin* of oil per *eifah*.
And on the day of the New Moon it shall be a young bullock without blemish, six lambs, and a ram; they shall be unblemished.
And he shall prepare a meal offering of an *eifah* for the bullock and an *eifah* for the ram, and for the lambs according to what his hand can attain, with a *hin* of oil per *eifah*.
And when the prince enters, he shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate, and exit by the same way.

And when the people of the land enter to prostrate themselves before Hashem at the appointed festivals, he who enters by way of the north gate to prostrate himself shall exit by way of the south gate; and he who enters by way of the south gate shall exit by way of the north gate. He shall not return by way of the gate through which he entered, but shall go out straight ahead.
And the prince shall be in their midst: when they enter, he shall enter; and when they exit, they shall exit together.

And at the feasts and appointed festivals, the meal offering shall be an *eifah* for a bullock and an *eifah* for a ram, and for the lambs according to what his hand can attain, with a *hin* of oil per *eifah*.

And when the prince prepares a voluntary offering—a burnt offering or peace offerings as a voluntary gift before Hashem—the gate that faces east shall be opened for him, and he shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings just as he does on the Shabbos day; then he shall go forth, and the gate shall be locked after his exit.
And a lamb in its first year without blemish you shall prepare as a daily burnt offering to Hashem; morning by morning you shall prepare it.

And a meal offering you shall prepare with it morning by morning: a sixth of an *eifah*, and a third of a *hin* of oil to moisten the fine flour—a meal offering to Hashem, an everlasting decree continually.
They shall prepare the lamb, the meal offering, and the oil morning by morning as a continual burnt offering.
Thus said Hashem Elokim: If the prince gives a gift out of his inheritance to any of his sons, it shall belong to his sons; it shall be their possession as an inheritance.

But if he gives a gift out of his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall belong to him until the Jubilee year (*Shattah d'Yovela*), and then return to the prince; only his inheritance given to his sons shall remain theirs permanently.

And the prince shall not take from the inheritance of the people to wrong them out of their possession; out of his own possession he shall provide an inheritance for his sons, so that My people shall not be scattered, every man from his possession.
Then he brought me through the entry passage beside the gate into the holy chambers of the Kohanim facing north; and behold, there was a place at the western end of them.

And he said to me: "This is the place where the Kohanim shall cook the guilt offering (*Asham*) and the sin offering (*Chatas*), and where they shall bake the meal offering (*Minchah*), so as not to carry them out into the outer courtyard to mingle with the people."
Then he led me out into the outer courtyard and brought me past the four corners of the courtyard; and behold, in every corner of the courtyard there was a smaller court.
In the four corners of the courtyard were enclosed courts, forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide; all four corner courts had the same measurement.
And there was a row of masonry walls built around all four of them, and cooking places were made at the bottom of the masonry walls all around.
And he said to me: "These are the cooking places where the ministers of the House shall cook the holy sacrifices of the people."

And he brought me back to the entrance of the House, and behold, water was issuing from beneath the threshold of the House toward the east—for the facade of the House faced east—and the water was flowing down from beneath the right side of the threshold of the House, south of the Altar.
Then he led me out by way of the north gate and led me around on the outside to the outer gate facing east; and behold, water was trickling from the right side.
When the man went out toward the east with a measuring line in his hand, he measured a thousand cubits, and led me through the water—water that reached the ankles.
Again he measured a thousand cubits, and led me through the water—water that reached the knees; again he measured a thousand cubits, and led me through—water that reached the loins.
Afterward he measured a thousand cubits—it was a river that I could not cross, for the water had grown deep, water to swim in, a river that could not be crossed on foot.
And he said to me: "Have you seen this, ben adam?" Then he led me and brought me back to the bank of the river.
As I returned, behold, along the bank of the river were very many trees on this side and on that side.
And he said to me: "These waters flow out toward the eastern region, flow down into the plain, and enter the sea; into the Great Sea they flow, and the waters shall be healed.

And it shall come to pass that every living creature that swarms, wherever the waters of the river come, shall live; and there shall be an abundance of fish, for these waters come there and heal, and everything shall live wherever the river comes.
And fishers shall stand beside it from Ein Gedi to Ein Eglaim; it shall be a place for spreading nets. Their fish shall be according to their kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, exceedingly many.
Its swamps and its marshes shall not be healed; they shall be left for salt pits.

And along the river, on its bank on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for food, whose leaves shall not wither, nor shall their fruit fail. Month by month they shall yield fresh fruit, for their waters issue from the Sanctuary; their fruit shall be for food, and their leaves for healing.
Thus said Hashem Elokim: This shall be the border by which you shall divide the land for an inheritance to the twelve tribes of Yisrael; Yosef shall receive two portions.
And you shall inherit it, one as well as his brother, as I swore by My word to give it to your fathers; and this land shall fall to you for an inheritance.
And this shall be the border of the land on the north side: from the Great Sea, by way of Chetlon, as one goes to Tzedad;
Chamas, Berosah, Sivrayim (which is between the border of Damascus and the border of Chamas), and Berekhas HaAgvai (which is on the border of Chavran).
And the border from the sea shall be Chatzar Einon, the border of Damascus, and northward to the north and the border of Chamas; this is the north side.
And on the east side: between Chavran, Damascus, Gilead, and the land of Yisrael, the Yarden shall be the border down to the eastern sea; this you shall measure as the east side.
And the south side southward: from Yericho to the waters of Merivas Rekem, the inheritance to the Great Sea; this is the south side southward.
And the west side shall be the Great Sea, from the border as far as opposite the entrance to Chamas; this is the west side.
So shall you divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Yisrael.

And it shall come to pass that you shall divide it by lot for an inheritance to yourselves and to the converts who dwell among you, who have begotten children among you; and they shall be to you as native-born among the Bnei Yisrael; with you they shall receive an inheritance among the tribes of Yisrael.
And in whatever tribe the convert resides, there shall you give him his inheritance, says Hashem Elokim."

And these are the names of the tribes from the northern border, along the way of Chetlon as one enters Chamas, to Chatzar Einan on the border of Damascus northward, beside the border of Chamas, extending from the east side to the west side: Dan, one portion.
And adjacent to the border of Dan, from the east side to the west side: Asher, one portion.
And adjacent to the border of Asher, from the east side to the west side: Naftali, one portion.
And adjacent to the border of Naftali, from the east side to the west side: Menasheh, one portion.
And adjacent to the border of Menasheh, from the east side to the west side: Efraim, one portion.
And adjacent to the border of Efraim, from the east side to the west side: Reuven, one portion.
And adjacent to the border of Reuven, from the east side to the west side: Yehudah, one portion.

And adjacent to the border of Yehudah, from the east side to the west side, shall be the set portion (*terumah*) that you shall set apart: twenty-five thousand reeds in width, and in length like one of the tribal portions from the east side to the west side; and the open space of the Sanctuary shall be in its midst.
The set portion that you shall set apart before Hashem shall be twenty-five thousand reeds in length, and ten thousand in width.

And for these shall be the holy set portion for the Kohanim: to the north twenty-five thousand, to the west a width of ten thousand, to the east a width of ten thousand, and to the south a length of twenty-five thousand; and the open space of the Sanctuary of Hashem shall be in its midst.
It shall be for the sanctified Kohanim of the sons of Tzadok, who kept the charge of My word, who did not go astray in the error of the Bnei Yisrael as the Levites went astray.
And it shall belong to them as a set portion out of the set portion of the land, a holy of holies, adjacent to the border of the Levites.

And the Levites shall have, parallel to the border of the Kohanim, twenty-five thousand reeds in length and ten thousand in width; the whole length shall be twenty-five thousand, and the width ten thousand.
And they shall not sell any of it, nor exchange it, nor transfer the choice part of the land; for it is holy before Hashem.

And the five thousand reeds that remain in width, along the front of the twenty-five thousand, shall be a profane area for the city—for dwellings and open space; and the open space of the city shall be in its midst.

And these shall be its measurements: the north side four thousand five hundred, the south side four thousand five hundred, the east side four thousand five hundred, and the west side four thousand five hundred.

And the open surrounding area for the city shall be two hundred and fifty reeds to the north, two hundred and fifty to the south, two hundred and fifty to the east, and two hundred and fifty to the west.

And the remainder in length, parallel to the holy set portion, shall be ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west, parallel to the holy set portion; and its produce shall serve for food for those who labor in the city.
And those who labor in the city shall cultivate it, drawn from all the tribes of Yisrael.
The entire set portion shall be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand reeds, square; you shall set apart the holy portion together with the possession of the city.

And the remainder shall belong to the prince (*Nasi*), on both sides of the holy set portion and the possession of the city, along the front of the twenty-five thousand reeds of the set portion to the eastern border, and westward along the front of the twenty-five thousand to the western border, corresponding to the tribal portions, for the prince; and the holy set portion and the open space of the Sanctuary of the House shall be in its midst.

Thus the possession of the Levites and the possession of the city shall be in the middle of that which belongs to the prince; between the border of Yehudah and the border of Binyamin shall belong to the prince.
As for the rest of the tribes, from the east side to the west side: Binyamin, one portion.
And adjacent to the border of Binyamin, from the east side to the west side: Shimon, one portion.
And adjacent to the border of Shimon, from the east side to the west side: Yissachar, one portion.
And adjacent to the border of Yissachar, from the east side to the west side: Zevulun, one portion.
And adjacent to the border of Zevulun, from the east side to the west side: Gad, one portion.
And adjacent to the border of Gad, at the south side southward, the border shall be from Yericho to the waters of Merivas Rekem, the inheritance to the Great Sea.
This is the land that you shall divide by lot for an inheritance to the tribes of Yisrael, and these are their portions, says Hashem Elokim.
And these are the exits of the city: on the north side, four thousand five hundred reeds by measure.
And the gates of the city shall be named after the tribes of Yisrael; three gates to the north: the gate of Reuven, one; the gate of Yehudah, one; the gate of Levi, one.
And at the east side, four thousand five hundred reeds; and three gates: the gate of Yosef, one; the gate of Binyamin, one; the gate of Dan, one.
And at the south side, four thousand five hundred reeds by measure; and three gates: the gate of Shimon, one; the gate of Yissachar, one; the gate of Zevulun, one.
At the west side, four thousand five hundred reeds, with their three gates: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; the gate of Naftali, one.
All around it shall be eighteen thousand reeds; and the name of the city, declared from the day that Hashem rests His Shechinah there, shall be: **Hashem Shammah** ("Hashem is there").
